No, not all prime numbers are even. Prime numbers are defined as natural numbers greater than 1 that have no positive divisors other than 1 and themselves. Examples of prime numbers include 3, 5, 7, 11, etc.

Odd prime numbers, which are prime numbers that cannot be divided evenly by 2, include the number 3, but no other odd prime numbers exist because they would have to be divisible by 2. Therefore, all prime numbers except 2 are even.
